questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction while driving is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes, which can damage property, injure people, or cause death.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights and a siren. You should:

options.text: Move to the right edge and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. This includes police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using sirens, horns, or red or blue lights. When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, pull to the right edge of the road as far as possible and stop.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol content (BAC) goes up, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and pass many vehicles, you will:

options.text: Reach your destination much faster and safer.
Increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other cars on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a vehicle, your chance of a crash increases.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less traction than paved roads. You must slow down when driving on gravel or dirt. Your stopping distance will be longer and skidding while turning is easier.

questions.question: If your car breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on a highway, make sure other drivers can see it. Get your car off the road and away from traffic if you can. Turn on your emergency lights to show you need help.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have put on their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Make a habit before starting your car. Put on your safety belt and make sure all passengers put on theirs too.

questions.question: When a blind person with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always let them cross first.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only need to let them cross at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always let them cross first.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind people may carry a white cane or use a guide dog. You must always let them cross first, no matter where they are crossing.

questions.question: If you get tired while driving, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and rest or switch drivers. Being tired makes it harder to think and slows your reactions, which makes driving dangerous.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower your blood alcohol content (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, lowers concentration, slows your reaction time, and greatly reduces coordination.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are what color?
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: What does this yellow pennant-shaped sign say?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped yellow signs mark a no passing zone.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean it is illegal to pass. You are in an area with limited visibility where passing another vehicle would be unsafe.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and vehicle speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and vehicle speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because of reduced visibility. It is difficult to judge distances and the speeds of other vehicles. You can only see as far as your headlights allow.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: What is an important step before turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Then adjust your speed to complete the turn safely.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming conditions like traffic direction changes, steep grades, or hazards that need your attention.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection if it is safe and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection if it is safe and clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you may proceed through the intersection. First, let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection pass. Then go when the way is clear.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving dangerous?

options.text: It makes you worry about the call cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
Other drivers pay attention to you using it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phones are dangerous because they take your eyes, hands, and mind off driving. Even skilled drivers have more crashes when they use a cell phone while driving.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and weakens your judgment.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has stopped with red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights, you must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: What should you do if you meet an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: The safest thing to do with an aggressive driver is to get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers. Respect all road users and follow the rules to stay safe.
